Alveolar type 2 (AT2) cell.description: Surfactant-producing alveolar epithelial cells responsible for reducing alveolar surface tension and supporting epithelial repair.

Activated or transitional AT2 cell.description: Stress-responsive AT2-derived cells that transiently acquire a KRT8-positive transitional state during alveolar injury and regeneration.

Alveolar type 1 (AT1) cell.description: Extremely thin gas-exchange epithelial cells forming most of the alveolar surface and closely neighboring AT2 cells.

Club and distal airway secretory cell.description: Secretory airway epithelial cells that produce protective mucins and antimicrobial factors and can be mistaken for distal alveolar epithelial cells.

Alveolar adventitial fibroblast.description: A matrix-producing distal lung fibroblast population associated with alveolar interstitium, extracellular matrix organization, and paracrine support of alveolar epithelium.

Alveolar lipofibroblast.description: A lipid-storing alveolar fibroblast that supports type II alveolar epithelial cells and contributes to surfactant homeostasis and alveolar repair.

Alveolar myofibroblast.description: A contractile, matrix-remodeling fibroblast involved in alveolar septal development, wound repair, and fibrotic remodeling.

Pulmonary pericyte.description: A mural cell surrounding pulmonary microvessels that regulates capillary stability, vascular tone, and endothelial barrier function and may be confused with contractile fibroblasts.

FABP4+ resident alveolar macrophage.description: Long-lived lung-resident alveolar macrophages specialized for surfactant catabolism, lipid handling, and maintenance of alveolar homeostasis.

FCN1+/SPP1+ monocyte-derived inflammator.description: Recently recruited monocyte-derived macrophages that display inflammatory, antigen-processing, and tissue-remodeling programs during lung injury or infection.

FOLR2+/LYVE1+ interstitial macrophage.description: Perivascular and interstitial macrophages that support stromal immune regulation, scavenging, and tissue remodeling rather than surfactant clearance.

CD1C+ conventional dendritic cell.description: Antigen-presenting conventional dendritic cells that can resemble macrophages but are distinguished by strong MHC class II, CD1C, and dendritic-cell lectin programs.

Alveolar fibroblast.description: Interstitial fibroblasts in the alveolar compartment that produce extracellular matrix and support alveolar epithelial and vascular homeostasis.

Adventitial fibroblast.description: COL15A1- and PI16-expressing fibroblasts located around larger vessels and airways that organize stromal niches and extracellular matrix.

Alveolar lipofibroblast.description: Lipid-storing alveolar fibroblasts that support surfactant production and alveolar type 2 cell function through PPARG-dependent metabolic programs.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile matrix-producing fibroblasts involved in alveolar septal remodeling, wound repair, and pulmonary fibrosis.

Alveolar type 1 epithelial cell.description: Highly flattened gas-exchange epithelial cells forming most of the alveolar surface and expressing AGER, CAV1, and AQP5 rather than fibroblast extracellular-matrix programs.

Naive/follicular B cell.description: Antigen-inexperienced mature B cells characterized by IgD expression, robust MHC class II antigen presentation, and TCL1A or FCER2 expression.

Memory B cell.description: Previously antigen-experienced B cells showing enhanced activation and antigen-presentation programs with variable class-switched or unswitched immunoglobulin expression.

Plasma cell.description: Terminally differentiated antibody-secreting cells with expanded endoplasmic reticulum, unfolded-protein-response machinery, and abundant immunoglobulin transcripts.

T cell (common neighboring type).description: T lymphocytes can be mistaken for B cells in sparse lymphoid preparations but are distinguished by CD3-complex and T-cell receptor transcripts rather than CD79A, MS4A1, or CD74.

MUC5AC-positive goblet cell.description: Mucus-producing airway secretory cells characterized by abundant MUC5AC, secretory-pathway genes, and goblet differentiation driven by SPDEF.

MUC5B-positive mucous secretory cell.description: MUC5B-enriched secretory epithelial cells that contribute to airway mucus and are common in distal conducting-airway and remodeled lung epithelium.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated bronchiolar secretory cells involved in epithelial maintenance and xenobiotic metabolism, typically marked by SCGB1A1 and CYP2F1.

Ciliated airway epithelial cell.description: Multiciliated airway cells specialized for mucociliary clearance and distinguished by FOXJ1-driven axonemal and ciliary assembly programs.

Basal airway epithelial cell.description: Airway progenitor cells that anchor to the basement membrane and regenerate secretory and ciliated epithelium, marked by TP63 and keratins KRT5/KRT14.

Bronchial_adventitial_fibroblast.description: A matrix-producing fibroblast population enriched around bronchi and vessels, characterized by COL14A1, COL15A1, PI16, and complement-associated extracellular matrix programs.

Alveolar_lipofibroblast.description: An alveolar interstitial fibroblast or lipofibroblast population supporting epithelial niche signaling and alveolar development, with WNT, FGF, and lipid-handling programs.

Myofibroblast.description: An activated contractile fibroblast state involved in matrix remodeling and fibrosis, marked by ACTA2, TAGLN, POSTN, CTHRC1, and collagen production.

Pericyte.description: A mural cell population surrounding pulmonary microvessels that can resemble fibroblasts but is distinguished by RGS5, CSPG4, PDGFRB, MCAM, and vascular contractility programs.

Airway tuft/brush cell (tuft-1, choliner.description: A rare chemosensory airway epithelial cell with a POU2F3-TRPM5 program and prominent cholinergic signaling machinery.

Airway tuft/brush cell (tuft-2, eicosano.description: A tuft-cell state specialized for epithelial immune communication through IL-25 production and eicosanoid biosynthesis.

Pulmonary neuroendocrine cell.description: A neuroendocrine airway epithelial cell that produces peptide hormones and neurotransmitters and is defined by ASCL1-INSM1 and dense-core vesicle programs.

Club cell.description: A secretory bronchiolar epithelial cell involved in airway protection, xenobiotic metabolism, and production of SCGB1A1-rich secretions.

Ciliated airway epithelial cell.description: A multiciliated airway epithelial cell specialized for mucociliary clearance through coordinated axonemal beating.

Aerocyte capillary endothelial cell (CAP.description: Specialized thin-walled aerocyte capillaries form the gas-exchange interface of alveoli and characteristically express CA4, EDNRB, TBX2, and SOSTDC1.

General capillary endothelial cell (CAP2.description: General capillary endothelial cells support alveolar perfusion and vascular homeostasis and are marked by GPIHBP1, FABP4, FCN3, and RGCC.

Arterial endothelial cell.description: Arterial endothelial cells line higher-pressure pulmonary arteries and display arterial specification programs driven by EFNB2, SOX17, GJA5, and NOTCH signaling.

Venous and postcapillary venular endothe.description: Venous and postcapillary venular endothelial cells mediate leukocyte trafficking and fluid exchange and commonly express ACKR1, COL15A1, SELE, and VCAM1.

Lymphatic endothelial cell.description: Lymphatic endothelial cells drain interstitial fluid and immune cells from the lung and are distinguished by PROX1, PDPN, FLT4, LYVE1, and CCL21.

Conventional CD1c-positive cDC2.description: A homeostatic conventional dendritic-cell population specialized for antigen presentation and commonly marked by CD1C, CLEC10A, FCER1A, and CD1E.

CD14-positive DC3.description: A monocyte-related CD1c-positive dendritic-cell state with inflammatory and phagocytic features that bridges conventional cDC2 and monocyte programs.

Migratory or activated cDC2.description: An activated dendritic-cell state enriched for costimulation, inflammatory chemokines, and CCR7-dependent migration toward lymphoid compartments.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: A type I interferon-producing dendritic-cell lineage defined by CLEC4C, IL3RA, GZMB, TCF4, and PLD4 rather than the CD1C-positive cDC2 program.

FCN1-positive classical monocyte.description: A circulating inflammatory myeloid population that can resemble CD14-positive DC3 but is distinguished by strong FCN1, S100A8/S100A9, LYZ, and VCAN expression.

CD4 naive and central-memory T cell.description: A relatively quiescent CD4 T-cell population with lymphoid homing, self-renewal, and antigen-inexperienced or central-memory features.

CD4 effector-memory and tissue-associate.description: An antigen-experienced CD4 population enriched for lung-tissue adaptation, cytokine responsiveness, and effector-memory or Th17-like programs.

Regulatory CD4 T cell.description: An immunosuppressive CD4 lineage characterized by FOXP3-dependent regulatory function and high expression of IL2RA, CTLA4, and activation-associated checkpoint molecules.

CD8 cytotoxic T cell.description: A neighboring conventional T-cell population expressing CD8 coreceptors and a stronger cytotoxic effector program than typical CD4 T cells.

Natural killer cell.description: An innate-like cytotoxic lymphocyte population that can be confused with activated CD4 or CD8 T cells but is distinguished by strong NK receptor and granule-mediated killing programs.

Naive_or_central_memory_CD8_T_cell.description: Antigen-inexperienced or recently activated CD8 T cells with lymphoid homing, self-renewal, and T-cell stemness programs.

Cytotoxic_effector_CD8_T_cell.description: Differentiated CD8 T cells specialized for target-cell killing and inflammatory cytokine production.

Lung_tissue_resident_memory_CD8_T_cell.description: Lung-retained CD8 T cells marked by tissue residency, epithelial interaction, local activation, and rapid recall capacity.

Mucosal_associated_invariant_T_cell.description: Innate-like CD8 or double-negative T cells expressing a semi-invariant TRAV1-2 T-cell receptor and mucosal antimicrobial effector programs.

Natural_killer_cell.description: Innate cytotoxic lymphocytes that resemble effector CD8 T cells but preferentially express NK receptors and TYROBP-FCER1G signaling genes.

CD14+ classical monocyte.description: Inflammatory circulating monocytes enriched for S100A8/S100A9 and FCN1 that enter lung tissue during homeostasis or inflammation.

CD14+FCGR3A+ intermediate monocyte.description: An antigen-presentation-competent transitional monocyte state combining CD14-associated inflammatory features with emerging FCGR3A and HLA class II expression.

FCGR3A+ non-classical monocyte.description: Patrolling monocytes characterized by high FCGR3A and MS4A7 expression with reduced S100A8/S100A9 inflammatory signatures.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Resident lung macrophages specialized for surfactant handling and alveolar homeostasis, expressing FABP4, PPARG, NAPSA, and MARCO.

Canonical club cells.description: Canonical non-ciliated airway secretory cells characterized by high SCGB1A1 expression and xenobiotic-detoxification, epithelial-protective, and secretory programs.

SCGB3A1-high distal secretory cells.description: Distal airway secretory cells enriched for SCGB3A1 and SCGB3A2 that populate respiratory bronchioles and represent a specialized club-like parenchymal compartment.

Goblet-like secretory cells.description: Mucus-producing secretory cells that can resemble club cells but show strong mucin, unfolded-protein-response, and secretory-granule programs.

Ciliated epithelial cells.description: Multiciliated airway epithelial cells defined by FOXJ1-dependent axoneme assembly and dynein-driven motility programs and commonly confused with club cells in low-RNA cells.

Basal epithelial cells.description: Airway progenitor cells with a keratin-rich basal program that may be mistaken for club cells because of shared KRT19 and epithelial-marker expression.

conventional dendritic cell type 1.description: Cross-presenting dendritic cells specialized for uptake of dead-cell material and activation of cytotoxic T-cell responses.

conventional dendritic cell type 2.description: Antigen-presenting CD1C-positive dendritic cells that coordinate helper T-cell and mucosal immune responses in the lung.

monocyte-derived dendritic cell_or_DC3.description: Inflammatory monocyte-derived antigen-presenting cells that resemble CD1C-positive dendritic cells but retain strong myeloid and monocyte-associated programs.

plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: Rare interferon-producing dendritic cells specialized for rapid type I interferon responses to viral and nucleic-acid sensing.

CLEC9A+ conventional dendritic cell (cDC.description: Cross-presenting conventional dendritic cells specialized for uptake of cell-associated antigens and priming of CD8+ T cells.

CD1C+ conventional dendritic cell (cDC2).description: Antigen-presenting conventional dendritic cells that promote CD4+ T-cell responses and are enriched at airway and parenchymal interfaces.

GZMB+ plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC).description: Specialized interferon-producing dendritic cells that respond rapidly to nucleic-acid sensing and viral inflammation.

CD14+ monocyte-derived dendritic cell (D.description: Inflammation-associated dendritic cells with mixed dendritic and monocyte features that accumulate in injured or inflamed lung tissue.

Alveolar macrophage.description: Resident lung macrophages that maintain alveolar surfactant homeostasis, clear particulates, and provide tissue immune surveillance.

SPP1+ monocyte-derived macrophage.description: A recruited macrophage population derived from circulating monocytes that accumulates in injured or inflamed lung and expresses lipid-processing, lysosomal, and osteopontin-associated programs.

FABP4+ resident alveolar macrophage.description: A long-lived, surfactant-adapted macrophage resident in the alveolar space and characterized by FABP4, PPARG, MARCO, and lipid-handling activity.

C1Q+ interstitial macrophage.description: A tissue-resident macrophage population located in the pulmonary interstitium that supports homeostasis, clearance, and immune regulation.

FCN1+ classical monocyte.description: A circulating or recently recruited inflammatory myeloid cell that can resemble an elicited macrophage but retains strong FCN1, S100A8/S100A9, VCAN, and CCR2 expression.

CD1C+ conventional dendritic cell.description: An antigen-presenting dendritic-cell population that may be confused with macrophages because of shared HLA class II and lysosomal programs but is distinguished by CD1C, FCER1A, and CLEC10A.

CCL21-positive lymphatic capillary endot.description: A mature pulmonary lymphatic endothelial population specialized for chemokine production and immune-cell trafficking, characterized by strong CCL21, PDPN, LYVE1, and PROX1 expression.

LYVE1-positive lymphatic endothelial cel.description: A lymphatic capillary-like endothelial subtype involved in interstitial fluid and lipid transport, showing prominent LYVE1, FABP4, PDPN, FLT4, and PROX1 expression.

Aerocyte capillary endothelial cell.description: A specialized blood capillary endothelial population lining the alveolar gas-exchange surface and expressing the aerocyte program marked by EDNRB, CA4, TBX2, and FOXP2.

Arterial endothelial cell.description: A blood-vessel endothelial subtype associated with pulmonary arterial branches and characterized by EFNB2, SOX17, GJA5, DLL4, and FBLN5 expression.

Alveolar type 1 pneumocyte.description: Highly flattened gas-exchange cells lining alveolar walls and expressing AGER, CAV1, AQP5, and PDPN.

Alveolar type 2 pneumocyte.description: Surfactant-producing alveolar epithelial cells that maintain alveolar homeostasis and regenerate the epithelium after injury.

Ciliated airway epithelial cell.description: Motile-cilia-bearing airway cells specialized for mucociliary clearance of inhaled particles and mucus.

Club and secretory airway epithelial cel.description: Non-ciliated airway secretory cells that produce club-cell products, antimicrobial factors, and epithelial repair mediators.

Basal airway epithelial cell.description: Progenitor-like airway epithelial cells anchored to the basement membrane and capable of replenishing secretory and ciliated lineages.

Alveolar fibroblast.description: Interstitial fibroblasts positioned around alveoli that support epithelial maintenance and extracellular-matrix organization through PDGFRA-, WNT-, and FGF-associated programs.

Adventitial fibroblast.description: Fibroblasts associated with vascular and airway adventitia that express COL15A1, PI16, complement, and matrix-remodeling programs.

Lipofibroblast.description: Lipid-storing alveolar fibroblasts that support surfactant production and type II pneumocyte function through PPARG- and adipogenic metabolic programs.

Pericyte.description: Mural cells surrounding capillaries that regulate vascular stability and are commonly confused with fibroblasts because of shared extracellular-matrix and contractile gene expression.

Airway smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile smooth muscle cells of airway walls characterized by strong ACTA2, MYH11, TAGLN, and calcium-handling programs that can overlap with myofibroblasts.

Hematopoietic stem cell.description: Rare quiescent multipotent progenitors with self-renewal capacity and a primitive CD34-positive, KIT-positive stem-cell transcriptional program.

Multipotent progenitor.description: Less primitive hematopoietic progenitors retaining multilineage potential while expressing FLT3 and early lymphoid or myeloid priming programs.

Common myeloid progenitor.description: Myeloid-primed progenitors that give rise to granulocytic, monocytic, dendritic, and related innate immune lineages.

Common lymphoid progenitor.description: Early lymphoid-restricted progenitors with IL7R, FLT3, recombination, and immature B- or T-lineage gene programs.

Mast cell.description: Granulated resident lung immune cells that can be mistaken for KIT-positive progenitors but are distinguished by mast-cell proteases, histamine synthesis, and Fc receptor machinery.

Pulmonary ionocyte.description: A rare airway epithelial cell specialized for ion transport and luminal pH regulation, characterized by FOXI1, ASCL3, CFTR, and vacuolar ATPase expression.

Club cell.description: A non-ciliated secretory airway epithelial cell involved in xenobiotic metabolism, epithelial protection, and regeneration.

Goblet cell.description: A mucus-producing secretory epithelial cell enriched for mucin biosynthesis, unfolded-protein processing, and antimicrobial defense.

Ciliated cell.description: A multiciliated airway epithelial cell specialized for mucociliary clearance through coordinated axonemal beating.

alveolar macrophage.description: Resident phagocytes occupying the alveolar lumen that specialize in surfactant handling, lipid metabolism, and pulmonary immune surveillance.

interstitial macrophage.description: Tissue-resident macrophages located in the interstitium that exhibit reparative, scavenging, and lymphatic-associated programs.

monocyte-derived macrophage.description: Recently recruited inflammatory macrophages derived from circulating monocytes and characterized by antimicrobial, inflammatory, and tissue-remodeling programs.

CD1C-positive dendritic cell.description: Antigen-presenting conventional dendritic cells that can resemble macrophages but are distinguished by CD1C, FCER1A, CLEC10A, and strong MHC class II expression.

Capillary pericyte.description: Capillary pericytes are mural cells that envelop small pulmonary capillaries and exhibit strong RGS5, COX4I2, KCNJ8, and ABCC9 programs associated with vascular stabilization and oxygen sensing.

Matrix-associated pericyte.description: Matrix-associated pericytes retain canonical mural-cell identity while producing prominent vascular basement-membrane and extracellular-matrix components.

Vascular smooth muscle cell.description: Vascular smooth muscle cells are larger contractile mural cells surrounding pulmonary arteries and arterioles and are distinguished by strong ACTA2, TAGLN, MYH11, and CNN1 expression.

Perivascular fibroblast.description: Perivascular fibroblasts are stromal matrix-producing cells adjacent to pulmonary vessels that express collagen, decorin, lumican, and fibroblast-associated PDGFRA programs rather than canonical pericyte markers.

Mast cell (MC_T; tryptase-dominant).description: A mucosal-like lung mast-cell population dominated by tryptase expression and typically showing IL1RL1, SIGLEC6, and CD200R3.

Mast cell (MC_TC; tryptase-chymase).description: A mature connective-tissue-like mast-cell population with prominent CMA1, CTSG, and MRGPRX2 expression in addition to tryptases.

Basophil.description: A circulating granulocyte-like allergic effector cell that resembles mast cells but is characterized by IL3RA, CCR3, CLC, and generally low or absent KIT and CMA1.

Eosinophil.description: A granulocyte population enriched for eosinophil granule proteins and receptors such as RNASE3, PRG2, EPX, IL5RA, and SIGLEC8 rather than mast-cell proteases.

Quiescent pleural mesothelial cell.description: A relatively quiescent pleural or peripheral lung mesothelial population forming a serosal barrier and expressing mesothelial identity markers such as MSLN, WT1, UPK3B, and PDPN.

Activated inflammatory mesothelial cell.description: An injury- or inflammation-responsive mesothelial state retaining mesothelial markers while upregulating chemokines, adhesion molecules, matrix-remodeling genes, and NF-kB or interferon-response programs.

Lung fibroblast.description: A stromal fibroblast population commonly confused with mesothelium because of its peripheral lung location, but distinguished by extracellular-matrix, collagen, and fibroblast growth-factor programs.

Pulmonary vascular endothelial cell.description: A pulmonary capillary or vascular endothelial population that can be mistaken for mesothelium but shows strong vascular junction, endothelial receptor, and blood-vessel homeostasis programs.

MUC5AC+ goblet cell.description: MUC5AC-high airway goblet cells produce inducible mucins and secretory antimicrobial factors and are enriched in inflamed or remodeling distal-airway epithelium.

MUC5B+ goblet or mucous secretory cell.description: MUC5B-dominant secretory cells produce constitutive airway mucus and are particularly associated with distal bronchiolar and gland-associated mucous programs.

Club secretory cell.description: Club cells are non-ciliated bronchiolar secretory cells that produce SCGB1A1 and detoxification, epithelial-repair, and innate-defense factors.

Airway serous secretory cell.description: Serous secretory cells release watery antimicrobial and protease-inhibitory products and are distinguished from mucous cells by LYZ, SLPI, and BPIFA1 expression.

Ciliated epithelial cell.description: Ciliated epithelial cells are a commonly confused neighboring population defined by motile-cilium assembly and axonemal genes rather than mucin or secretory-product expression.

Mature multiciliated airway epithelial c.description: Terminally differentiated airway epithelial cells bearing motile cilia that propel mucus and inhaled particles toward the proximal airway.

Deuterosomal or early multiciliated airw.description: A transient multiciliating progenitor state characterized by deuterosome formation, centriole amplification, and ongoing cell-cycle activity before mature cilia assembly.

Club secretory airway cell.description: Non-ciliated secretory airway epithelial cells that produce protective proteins, detoxify inhaled compounds, and contribute to epithelial repair.

Goblet or mucus-secretory airway cell.description: Mucus-producing airway epithelial cells enriched for mucin biosynthesis, glycosylation, and secretory-granule programs.

Basal airway epithelial cell.description: Regenerative airway epithelial progenitors anchored to the basement membrane that replenish secretory and multiciliated lineages after injury.

Mature multiciliated epithelial cell.description: Fully differentiated airway multiciliated cells express FOXJ1-driven axonemal, basal-body, and ciliary motility programs that support mucociliary clearance.

Deuterosomal or early multiciliated epit.description: Deuterosomal and early multiciliated progenitors are cycling or differentiating epithelial cells initiating centriole amplification and the multiciliogenesis program.

Club secretory epithelial cell.description: Club cells are non-ciliated bronchiolar secretory epithelial cells specialized for xenobiotic metabolism, epithelial repair, and production of airway protective proteins.

Mucous or goblet secretory epithelial ce.description: Goblet and mucous secretory cells produce polymeric mucins and antimicrobial airway secretions and can be mistaken for ciliated cells during epithelial differentiation.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile extracellular-matrix-producing fibroblasts involved in alveolar interstitial remodeling and repair.

Alveolar Fibroblast.description: Noncontractile interstitial fibroblasts supporting alveolar structure and mesenchymal signaling, including fibroblast growth factor and WNT programs.

Adventitial Fibroblast.description: Perivascular and airway-adjacent fibroblasts characterized by COL15A1, PI16, complement, and matrix-support programs.

Pericyte.description: Mural cells that envelop pulmonary microvessels and regulate vascular stability, tone, and endothelial function.

Vascular Smooth Muscle Cell.description: Highly contractile cells of pulmonary arteries and larger vascular walls that can be mistaken for ACTA2-positive myofibroblasts.

MUC5AC-high goblet cell.description: A mucus-producing airway secretory cell characterized by strong MUC5AC, SPDEF, CLCA1, and AGR2 expression and commonly expanded during type 2 inflammation.

MUC5B-high mucous secretory cell.description: A mucous secretory epithelial subtype enriched for MUC5B and BPIFB1 that contributes to constitutive airway mucus production and overlaps transcriptionally with goblet cells.

Club cell.description: A non-ciliated airway secretory and detoxifying cell marked by SCGB1A1 and SCGB3A1, often confused with mucous goblet cells because of shared epithelial and secretory programs.

Ciliated airway epithelial cell.description: A multiciliated airway epithelial cell defined by FOXJ1-driven motile cilia genes and commonly mistaken for goblet or other epithelial cells when mucous and cilia transcripts are co-expressed.

CD56bright natural killer cell.description: Less terminally differentiated NK cells enriched for cytokine production, lymphoid tissue homing, and relatively modest cytotoxicity.

CD56dim cytotoxic natural killer cell.description: Mature circulating and tissue-infiltrating NK cells with strong granule-mediated cytotoxicity and high expression of killer receptors.

Adaptive or memory-like natural killer c.description: Antigen-experienced NK cells characterized by NKG2C expression, durable effector features, and enhanced responsiveness to viral or inflammatory stimulation.

Cytotoxic T lymphocyte.description: T-cell receptor-positive cytotoxic lymphocytes that can resemble NK cells but retain consistent CD3 and TCR-chain expression.

Non-classical monocytes.description: Patrolling blood-derived monocytes enriched for FCGR3A, LST1, MS4A7, LILRB1, and CDKN1C that survey the pulmonary microvasculature and parenchyma.

Intermediate monocytes.description: A transitional monocyte population expressing both CD14-associated inflammatory genes and FCGR3A-associated antigen-presentation and phagocytic programs.

Classical monocytes.description: Recently recruited inflammatory monocytes marked by S100A8, S100A9, LYZ, FCN1, VCAN, and CD14.

Alveolar macrophages.description: Lung-resident macrophages specialized for surfactant clearance and lipid homeostasis, characterized by FABP4, PPARG, INPP4B, MARCO, and C1Q genes.

Conventional dendritic cells.description: Antigen-presenting myeloid cells that can resemble monocytes but are distinguished by CD1C, FCER1A, CLEC10A, and strong MHC class II expression.

IgA plasma cell.description: Mucosal antibody-secreting plasma cells specialized for production of polymeric IgA and commonly enriched near airway and alveolar surfaces.

IgG plasma cell.description: Class-switched plasma cells producing IgG, often associated with systemic or chronic pulmonary immune responses.

IgM plasma cell.description: Less class-switched antibody-secreting cells that retain prominent IgM expression and may represent early or locally maintained plasma-cell responses.

Plasmablast.description: Recently activated and often proliferating antibody-secreting precursors that retain plasma-cell secretory programs but show stronger cell-cycle activity.

Memory B cell.description: Antigen-presenting mature B cells that can be mistaken for plasma cells when immunoglobulin transcripts are abundant but lack the full unfolded-protein-response and secretory machinery.

Resting plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: A quiescent pDC population specialized for rapid type I interferon production and characterized by CLEC4C, IL3RA, GZMB, GZMB, TCF4, and GZMB expression.

Interferon-activated plasmacytoid dendri.description: An activated pDC state induced by viral or inflammatory signals and marked by strong interferon-stimulated gene expression while retaining CLEC4C and IL3RA.

AXL-positive SIGLEC6-positive dendritic.description: A transitional pDC-like dendritic population expressing AXL and SIGLEC6 that can be mistaken for either conventional pDCs or CD1C-positive dendritic cells.

CD1C-positive conventional dendritic cel.description: The major conventional dendritic-cell population in lung parenchyma, specialized for antigen uptake and presentation and commonly confused with pDCs because of shared HLA class II expression.

Monocyte-derived dendritic cell.description: An inflammatory monocyte-derived antigen-presenting cell with strong myeloid and lysosomal programs that can resemble activated pDCs or conventional dendritic cells in inflamed lung tissue.

Alveolar type 1 epithelial cell.description: Highly flattened gas-exchange cells that form most of the alveolar surface and express AGER, CAV1, PDPN, AQP5, and HOPX.

Alveolar type 2 epithelial cell.description: Surfactant-producing alveolar progenitor cells that maintain epithelial homeostasis and can differentiate into type 1 cells.

KRT8-positive transitional alveolar epit.description: An injury-associated intermediate alveolar epithelial state characterized by keratin induction, epithelial remodeling, and reduced mature AT1 or AT2 identity.

Club-like bronchiolar secretory cell.description: Non-ciliated bronchiolar secretory epithelial cells that produce airway-protective proteins and are a frequent source of confusion with alveolar epithelial populations.

Canonical alveolar type 1 epithelial cel.description: Highly flattened gas-exchange epithelial cells specialized for maintaining the alveolar air-blood barrier and expressing AGER, CAV1, PDPN, and AQP5.

Interferon-stimulated alveolar type 1 ce.description: An alveolar type 1 state retaining epithelial gas-exchange markers while showing strong type I or type II interferon-response activation.

Alveolar epithelial transitional KRT8-po.description: A reparative alveolar epithelial intermediate often arising during injury, characterized by keratin remodeling, epithelial activation, and incomplete differentiation toward type 1 cells.

Alveolar type 2 epithelial cell.description: Surfactant-producing cuboidal alveolar epithelial cells that serve as progenitors for type 1 cells and express SFTPC, ABCA3, SFTPA1, and NAPSA.

Aerocyte capillary endothelial cell.description: A specialized alveolar capillary endothelial subtype closely apposed to type 1 epithelium and marked by CA4, EDNRB, EMCN, FCN3, and RGCC.

Canonical alveolar type 2 cell.description: Specialized surfactant-producing alveolar epithelial cells that maintain distal lung homeostasis and regenerate alveolar epithelium.

Stress or injury-associated transitional.description: An activated alveolar type 2 state arising during epithelial injury and repair, characterized by reduced mature surfactant identity and induction of stress, remodeling, and transitional programs.

Proliferating alveolar type 2 cell.description: A cycling alveolar type 2 population that retains alveolar epithelial identity while undergoing cell division during homeostasis or repair.

Alveolar type 1 cell.description: Extremely thin gas-exchange epithelial cells specialized for respiratory surface formation and alveolar-capillary diffusion.

Club or bronchiolar secretory cell.description: Non-ciliated bronchiolar secretory epithelial cells that produce airway-protective secretions and can overlap transcriptionally with activated alveolar epithelial cells.

Pulmonary arterial endothelial cell.description: Arterial endothelial cells lining pulmonary arteries express arterial specification programs driven by EFNB2, SOX17, GJA5, DLL4, and FBLN5.

Pulmonary capillary aerocyte endothelial.description: Aerocyte-like capillary endothelial cells form the gas-exchange interface and are marked by EDNRB, TBX2, CA4, EMCN, GPIHBP1, and SOSTDC1.

Pulmonary venous endothelial cell.description: Pulmonary venous and post-capillary endothelial cells display venous identity and inflammatory adhesion programs characterized by ACKR1, NR2F2, COL15A1, SELP, and VCAM1.

Pulmonary vascular pericyte.description: Pulmonary vascular pericytes are mural cells surrounding endothelial tubes and express RGS5, PDGFRB, CSPG4, MCAM, NOTCH3, and contractile genes.

Pulmonary neuroendocrine cell (PNEC), AS.description: A canonical pulmonary neuroendocrine population with strong neuroendocrine differentiation and ASCL1-INSM1 transcriptional activity.

Pulmonary neuroendocrine cell (PNEC), CA.description: A peptide-secreting PNEC state enriched for CALCA, CALCB, GRP and related neuropeptide-processing programs.

Pulmonary tuft cell.description: A rare chemosensory epithelial cell type marked by POU2F3-TRPM5 signaling, taste-transduction machinery and type 2 immune-modulating cytokine production.

Pulmonary club cell.description: A bronchiolar secretory epithelial population producing SCGB1A1 and xenobiotic-detoxification, mucosal-defense and epithelial-repair programs.

Canonical airway basal cell.description: A self-renewing airway epithelial progenitor population expressing TP63, KRT5, and KRT14 that gives rise to secretory and ciliated epithelial cells.

Injury-activated or suprabasal basal cel.description: A stressed, repair-associated basal state with enhanced keratinization, epithelial remodeling, and inflammatory-response programs.

Cycling basal cell.description: A proliferating airway basal progenitor population retaining basal-cell identity while expressing strong DNA-replication and mitotic programs.

Club secretory cell.description: A nonciliated secretory airway epithelial cell producing club-cell secretoglobins and xenobiotic, mucosal, and epithelial maintenance factors.

Ciliated epithelial cell.description: A terminally differentiated mucociliary epithelial cell characterized by motile cilia assembly and axonemal motor programs.

Respiratory tract hillock cell.description: A specialized keratinized, suprabasal airway epithelial population marked by strong KRT13/KRT4/KRT16 expression and epithelial stress-barrier programs.

Airway basal cell.description: A regenerative airway stem/progenitor population forming the basal layer and expressing TP63, KRT5, KRT14, and basement-membrane adhesion genes.

Suprabasal squamous airway epithelial ce.description: A differentiating squamous or suprabasal airway population that overlaps with hillock cells but shows stronger cornification and epidermal barrier maturation.

Club secretory cell.description: A non-ciliated secretory airway epithelial population producing club-cell secretoglobins, antiproteases, mucosal factors, and xenobiotic-metabolism genes.

airway smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile smooth muscle cells forming the muscular walls of bronchi and bronchioles, characterized by strong actomyosin, calcium-handling, and airway-receptor programs.

vascular smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile mural cells surrounding pulmonary arteries and veins, showing a mature vascular smooth muscle program with MYH11, NOTCH3, MCAM, and calcium-channel expression.

pericyte.description: Perivascular capillary-associated mural cells that support endothelial tubes and are distinguished from true smooth muscle by RGS5, PDGFRB, CSPG4, KCNJ8, and COX4I2.

myofibroblast.description: Activated extracellular-matrix-producing stromal cells that can resemble smooth muscle through ACTA2 and TAGLN but are defined by collagen, fibronectin, and remodeling programs.

fibroblast.description: Interstitial lung matrix-producing cells that are commonly confused with smooth muscle when activated but lack a dominant contractile program and instead express collagen, decorin, lumican, and fibroblast-associated matrix genes.

Alveolar fibroblast.description: PDGFRA-positive interstitial fibroblasts situated around alveolar structures that support epithelial regeneration and extracellular-matrix organization.

Lipofibroblast.description: Lipid-handling alveolar fibroblasts that store neutral lipids and provide trophic support to neighboring alveolar type II epithelial cells.

Adventitial fibroblast.description: COL15A1-positive fibroblasts enriched in perivascular adventitia that organize connective tissue and regulate vascular and immune niches.

Myofibroblast.description: Contractile matrix-producing fibroblasts associated with tissue repair, airway and alveolar remodeling, and pulmonary fibrosis.

Pericyte.description: Mural cells wrapped around pulmonary microvessels that regulate capillary stability, permeability, and vascular tone and are commonly confused with fibroblasts.

CD4 memory T cells.description: Antigen-experienced or recirculating helper T cells with IL7R, CCR7, and TCF7 expression and limited cytotoxic activity.

CD8 tissue-resident cytotoxic T cells.description: Lung-resident CD8 T cells combining tissue-retention markers with granzyme-, perforin-, and chemokine-mediated cytotoxic programs.

Regulatory T cells.description: Immunosuppressive CD4 T cells characterized by FOXP3, high-affinity IL-2 receptor expression, and inhibitory or activation-associated receptors.

MAIT cells.description: Innate-like T cells recognizing microbial metabolites through MR1 and commonly expressing TRAV1-2, KLRB1, SLC4A10, and cytotoxic effector genes.

Natural killer cells.description: Cytotoxic innate lymphocytes that can be mistaken for T cells because of shared NKG7 and CD3-associated transcripts but typically show strong GNLY, TYROBP, FCGR3A, and KLRD1 expression.

MUC5AC-high airway goblet cell.description: Mucous secretory epithelial cells of proximal and transitional airways characterized by abundant MUC5AC production and goblet-cell differentiation.

MUC5B-high distal airway goblet cell.description: Mucous secretory cells enriched in distal bronchiolar and bronchial compartments, with prominent MUC5B expression and partial overlap with club-cell programs.

Club cell.description: Non-ciliated bronchiolar secretory progenitor cells that express SCGB1A1 and detoxification, epithelial-maintenance, and airway repair programs but little mucin.

Airway serous secretory cell.description: Protein-secreting airway epithelial cells that produce antimicrobial and protective factors such as lysozyme, lactoferrin, and secretory leukocyte protease inhibitor.

Multiciliated airway cell.description: Terminally differentiated airway epithelial cells bearing motile cilia and specialized axonemal and ciliogenesis machinery for mucociliary clearance.

Tracheobronchial airway smooth muscle ce.description: Contractile smooth muscle cells surrounding conducting airways and bronchi, specialized for regulation of airway caliber.

Pulmonary vascular smooth muscle cell.description: Contractile mural cells encircling pulmonary arteries and veins that control vascular tone and pulmonary vascular resistance.

Pulmonary pericyte.description: Perivascular mural cells associated primarily with capillaries and small vessels, supporting endothelial stability and microvascular integrity.

Pulmonary myofibroblast.description: Matrix-producing activated fibroblasts in the lung interstitium that combine extracellular-matrix secretion with partial contractile myofibroblast features.

Pulmonary fibroblast.description: Resident interstitial stromal cells that maintain lung extracellular matrix and can be mistaken for less activated smooth muscle or myofibroblast populations.

ACKR1-positive systemic venous and postc.description: Venular endothelial cells specialized for leukocyte recruitment and blood-tissue exchange, often marked by ACKR1, adhesion molecules, and COL15A1.

Pulmonary venous endothelial cells.description: Venous endothelial cells lining pulmonary veins and larger venular channels, with a venous transcriptional program and enhanced barrier and trafficking functions.

Arterial endothelial cells.description: Arterial endothelial cells are specialized for high-pressure blood flow and are distinguished by EFNB2, SOX17, GJA5, DLL4, and SEMA3G.

General and aerocyte pulmonary capillary.description: Pulmonary capillary endothelial cells form the gas-exchange interface and include CA4-positive aerocytes and GPIHBP1-positive general capillary cells.

Lymphatic endothelial cells.description: Lymphatic endothelial cells drain interstitial fluid and immune cells and are defined by PDPN, LYVE1, CCL21, FLT4, and PROX1.
